title: The modern church, looking back
hookLine: Tubman, Bonhoeffer, Romero, Tutu, and a global church
tomorrow: Christmas, or every Sunday: which one is the real feast?

cards: From the track, the people in the stands are a blur of color.

The letter to the Hebrews runs through a long list of the faithful, Abraham, Moses, Rahab and more, and then reaches for an odd word: “Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses.”
Then it tells the reader to lay aside every weight and run. A cloud? Why call a crowd of people who have already died a cloud?

teach.b: Hebrews doesn't explain the word, so readers offer answers. One: a cloud surrounds you. You don't watch it from a distance; you're inside it.
Two: a cloud is many drops that read as one, and the witnesses are many lives that read as one story. Either way, notice what they're for. They aren't judges waiting for someone to trip.

They ran first, and because they're there, the runner can lay aside the weight. And the cloud kept growing. Harriet Tubman escaped slavery, then went back to lead others out, and spoke of praying as she went.

Dietrich Bonhoeffer, a German Lutheran pastor, spoke against the Nazi regime and was executed by it. Óscar Romero, archbishop of San Salvador, spoke up for the poor and was shot while celebrating Mass.
Desmond Tutu, an Anglican archbishop, worked against apartheid in South Africa, and spoke of ubuntu, a word from southern Africa he explained roughly as: a person is a person through other people.
Different churches, countries, dangers. Behind them, a church praying in Lagos and Seoul, São Paulo and Manila. Some churches formally name saints; others remember their people in prayer and song.
Both keep the cloud in view.

how: Some churches remember modern martyrs and witnesses on set days of the year, and others name them in prayers, sermons and songs.

games.q: a classmate says saints are only a Catholic and Orthodox thing. a Baptist friend says her church remembers its heroes too. what fits Hebrews 12?
o: only officially named saints count as witnesses.
churches differ on naming saints, but each keeps a cloud who ran first.
remembering people is a distraction from the race.

practice: Write one name by hand: a modern witness from today, or someone from your own life whose faith or courage ran ahead of you, a grandparent, a teacher, a neighbor. Under it, write the one weight they helped you lay down.
If you pray, give thanks for them through the sit.

wordCard.voice: The modern church. Tubman, Bonhoeffer, Romero, Tutu, and a church praying in many languages: the cloud, still growing.

orig.note: Greek: a cloud, a great mass. Hebrews 12:1 uses it for the crowd of witnesses.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: the cloud of witnesses, who ran first so others could keep running. See you tomorrow.
